messages.author: d1cd3b8c586909ad
messages.subject: make graph list for vertex-wise group analysis
parts:
Dear Chris



I want to make graph list for vertex-wise group analysis


for brainGraph_GLM function, I have to make g.list. However I cannot fully understand about g.list

I have 100 matrices(3 groups) from tractography data
(subj001.mat, subj002.mat ... subj100.mat)
group1 : subj001~subj032 , group2 : subj033~subj065, group3 : subj066~subj100



-------------
flist=dir(pattern= "*.mat")
for(i in 1:length(flist)) { 
matfile=as.matrix(read.table(flist[i], header=F))
subjname=sub(pattern = "(.*)\\..*$",  replacement = "\\1", basename(flist[i]))
assign(subjname, graph_from_adjacency_matrix(adjmatrix = matfile, mode ="undirected",weighted =TRUE))
   
}
------------------------

using command above, I made 100 igraph objects in R environment(subj001, subj002, ... subj100)


In this situation, how can I make concatenated g.list for 3 groups  brainGraph_GLM? 
Is there any easy way to make g.list?

best
dohyun

messages.author: dadcb4fd6a01f8d1
messages.subject: Re: [brainGraph-help] make graph list for vertex-wise group analysis
parts:
Hi Dohyun,
Have you checked out the User Guide? Chapter 6 details how to create matrix and graph lists from tractography data. Specifically Chapter 6.2. It explains the function arguments and the different types of thresholded connectivity matrices
it will output. And then Chapter 6.3 gives code for creating the graph lists.

After you try the code, let me know if you have specific questions.
Chris

messages.author: dadcb4fd6a01f8d1
messages.subject: Re: [brainGraph-help] make graph list for vertex-wise group analysis
parts:
First, it is possible that the design matrix is rank-deficient. You may get the design matrix by:
X.design <- brainGraph_GLM_design(covars.dti[, c(1:2, 4), with=F], coding='cell.means')

And then inspect the output to make sure it is the correct design. At this point you should also ensure that the supplied contrast vector "c(0, 1, 0, 0)" is correct.

Second, you should make sure that "length(newG)" equals the total number of subjects in your study. If not, then the supplied graph list is incorrect (although it should have produced a specific error). You may also use the following code to concatenate all graphs of the first threshold:

newG <- do.call(Map, c(c, g.norm))[[1]]

----
What version of R and other packages are you using? You can find this out by typing one of the following 2 commands:

sessionInfo()
devtools::session_info()

You should first make sure all of your packages are the latest versions. For RcppEigen, I am using v0.3.3.3.0 and Rcpp is version 0.12.13. For "data.table", I am using v1.10.4.3. And for "igraph", I am using v1.1.2 (but this error is unrelated to "igraph"). The R version I am using is v3.4.1.

To update packages, you may use the command "update.packages()".

Chris
